fields.Trigger: Monthly billing cycle for monthly-payment subscribers

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts receivable, credit deferred revenue" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "post cash receipt — debit cash, credit AR" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconciles subscription billing vs. payments received" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Payment failure rate**: Philippine credit card auto-charge failure rates can be 5–10% (expired cards, insufficient funds); robust dunning process needed
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W267 (digital payment reconciliation) for payment matching

steps.activity: System generates monthly subscription charges: (a) for monthly-payment subscribers: auto-charge credit card or e-wallet on file, (b) billing date: 1st of month (or enrollment anniversary date), (c) amount: monthly subscription fee (annual fee ÷ 12), (d) GL posting: debit accounts receivable, credit deferred revenue

Payment processing: (a) credit card: auto-charge via payment gateway, (b) GCash/Maya: auto-debit via partner API, (c) success: post cash receipt — debit cash, credit AR, (d) failure: trigger dunning per W1986

Monthly reconciliation: (a) AR Clerk reconciles subscription billing vs. payments received, (b) failed payments: total failed charges and follow-up actions, (c) deferred revenue: new enrollments added, revenue recognized from completed visits, net deferred revenue balance

fields.Participants: Trade Account Manager, Sales Associate, Customer
fields.Trigger: Subscription approaching renewal date (30 days before)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-send of "sends renewal notice 30 days before expiry" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-remind of "reminder with incentive" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "discount on renewal for upgrade" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Renewal rate**: 70% target is ambitious for Philippine market where subscription fatigue is growing; continuous service quality essential for retention
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W17 (loyalty) for bonus points incentive

steps.activity: System sends renewal notice 30 days before expiry: (a) email + SMS to subscriber, (b) include: service summary (visits completed, remaining), renewal price, renewal options (same tier, upgrade, downgrade), easy-renew link for online payment

Follow-up sequence: (a) 30 days before: renewal notice, (b) 14 days before: second reminder with incentive (bonus loyalty points for early renewal), (c) 7 days before: final reminder, (d) expiry date: "Your subscription has expired — renew now to avoid service interruption"

Upsell during renewal: (a) if customer on basic tier: offer upgrade to standard (additional 15% discount on renewal for upgrade), (b) if customer has single service: offer bundle with second service at 20% discount, (c) Sales Associate in-store can also process renewal with upsell at POS

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, AR Clerk, Accounting Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-request of "Customer requests cancellation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Pro-rata refund calculation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track retention attempt outcome" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Refund disputes**: Customers may dispute refund calculation (especially a-la-carte rate vs. subscription rate for completed visits); clear subscription terms and transparent calculation essential
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W101 (customer refund) for refund processing

steps.activity: Customer requests cancellation: (a) channel: in-store, phone, email, online, (b) Customer Service Rep verifies identity and subscription details, (c) cancellation reason captured (mandatory): (i) service quality, (ii) price, (iii) no longer needed, (iv) moving, (v) competitor switch, (vi) other

Pro-rata refund calculation: (a) annual subscription: refund = (remaining unused months ÷ 12) × annual fee, less: (i) visits already completed at a-la-carte rate (if a-la-carte rate > subscription pro-rata rate), (ii) cancellation fee per subscription agreement (if applicable), (iii) promotional discount clawback (if customer received enrollment discount), (b) monthly subscription: cancel next billing cycle; no mid-month refund

Refund processing: (a) AR Clerk processes refund per W101 (customer refund & credit processing), (b) refund method: same as original payment (credit card → credit card refund; GCash → GCash refund; cash at POS → cash refund), (c) reverse deferred revenue for unused portion, (d) cancellation confirmation sent to customer via email

Retention attempt: (a) before processing cancellation, Customer Service Rep offers retention options: (i) service credit for next visit, (ii) temporary pause instead of cancellation, (iii) downgrade to lower tier, (b) track retention attempt outcome

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, AR Clerk, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer requests upgrade; system suggests upgrade based on usage

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-request of "Customer requests upgrade" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-calculate of "calculates price adjustment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "checklist provided to partner" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-383 (ensure controlled execution — Subscription Billing, Renewal & Lifecycle (PA-47.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Prorated pricing complexity**: Upgrade fee calculation must account for services already rendered at lower tier; system must handle edge cases
System Touchpoints: - Subscription tier change with pro-rata pricing (W1985.2)
- Integration with W282 (subscription billing) for billing adjustment

steps.activity: Customer requests upgrade: (a) from basic to standard or premium, (b) or from single service to bundle, (c) process via customer service, in-store POS, or online self-service

System calculates price adjustment: (a) upgrade fee = (new tier annual price − remaining credit from current tier), (b) prorated: based on months remaining in current subscription, (c) collect upgrade fee as additional payment, (d) adjust deferred revenue: increase by upgrade fee amount
Service partner notified of tier change: (a) higher tier includes more comprehensive service, (b) updated service checklist provided to partner, (c) next visit uses new tier scope

fields.Participants: AR Clerk, Customer Service Rep, Customer

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "System detects payment failure" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "update your payment method." (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Service interruption**: Suspending service visits due to payment failure may lead to customer churn; balance firm collection with retention
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W108 (collection escalation) for escalation path
Time Estimate: - Automated dunning; 10–15 min per manual call

steps.activity: System detects payment failure: (a) credit card declined, (b) e-wallet insufficient balance, (c) bank account issue, (d) system tags subscription as "payment due"

Dunning sequence: (a) Day 1: SMS notification — "Your payment didn't go through. Please update your payment method.", (b) Day 3: email with payment update link, (c) Day 7: customer service call, (d) Day 14: second call + final notice, (e) Day 30: subscription suspended (service visits paused)

Payment recovery: (a) customer updates payment method (online or in-store), (b) system retries charge, (c) if successful: reactivate subscription, clear overdue status, (d) if customer unresponsive after 60 days: auto-cancel subscription per W1984 (no refund — subscription was partially used)

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, AR Clerk, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer requests temporary pause (moving, travel, financial difficulty)
fields.Volume: ~5–10% of subscribers may pause per year

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-request of "Customer requests pause" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "System processes pause" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-send of "sends reactivation reminder 7 days before pause end date" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-383 (ensure controlled execution — Subscription Billing, Renewal & Lifecycle (PA-47.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pause abuse**: Customers may repeatedly pause to avoid payment; limit to 1 pause per subscription year
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W282 (subscription billing) for billing pause

steps.activity: Customer requests pause: (a) reason: travel, renovation, temporary move, financial difficulty, (b) pause duration: 1–6 months maximum, (c) Customer Service Rep verifies subscription is in good standing

System processes pause: (a) pause start date and end date recorded, (b) monthly billing suspended during pause period, (c) annual subscription: pause extends subscription expiry by pause duration, (d) service visits cancelled during pause, (e) customer notified of pause confirmation with reactivation date

Reactivation: (a) system sends reactivation reminder 7 days before pause end date, (b) customer confirms reactivation (or requests extension), (c) billing resumes, (d) next service visit scheduled, (e) if customer does not respond: auto-reactivate after 14 days grace period

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, AR Clerk, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer purchases subscription as gift; customer moves and transfers service

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-collect of "Gift subscription purchase" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validates new address against service territory" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-383 (ensure controlled execution — Subscription Billing, Renewal & Lifecycle (PA-47.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Recipient non-activation**: Gift recipient may not activate subscription; gift purchaser may request refund if unused after 90 days
System Touchpoints: - Gift subscription enrollment with recipient activation (W1988.1)
- Integration with W1979 (territory mapping) for coverage check

steps.activity: Gift subscription purchase: (a) customer purchases subscription at POS or online as gift, (b) recipient details collected: name, address, phone, email, (c) gift notification sent to recipient with activation instructions, (d) recipient activates by confirming address and scheduling first visit

Subscription transfer (customer moving): (a) customer requests transfer to new address, (b) system validates new address against service territory, (c) if covered: update service address and assign new service partner, (d) if not covered: offer cancellation with pro-rata refund or pause until coverage expands
Financial processing: (a) no fee for gift activation or address transfer, (b) service territory change may affect partner cost: internal cost reallocation, no customer price change

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-send of "sends automated communications at lifecycle events" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews communication effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-383 (ensure controlled execution — Subscription Billing, Renewal & Lifecycle (PA-47.2).)
- operational: CMO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Communication fatigue**: Too many messages lead to opt-outs; limit to essential lifecycle communications + 1 promotional message per month
System Touchpoints: - Automated communication engine with lifecycle triggers (W1989.1)
- Integration with W258 (omni-channel ticketing) for customer service escalation

steps.activity: System sends automated communications at lifecycle events: (a) enrollment confirmation with welcome guide, (b) service visit reminder: 48 hours and 2 hours before scheduled visit, (c) service completion confirmation with satisfaction survey, (d) renewal notice: 30/14/7 days before expiry, (e) payment confirmation (or failure notice), (f) subscription anniversary: thank you + loyalty points bonus

CMO designs communication templates: (a) consistent BuildRight branding, (b) SMS: concise (160 char), actionable, (c) email: branded template with service details and self-service links, (d) app push notification: quick-action buttons, (e) all communications comply with RA 10173 (consent-based)

Quarterly: CMO reviews communication effectiveness: (a) open rate, click rate, action rate per communication type, (b) A/B test subject lines and timing, (c) adjust communication frequency: reduce if opt-out rate > 2%/month
